title.narrative: Provision of life-saving primary health care services to La Nina conditions-affected populations in Qansah Dheere district, Bay region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis proposed 12-month health program aims to address the health needs and enhance the health status of La Nina-affected populations in Qansah Dheere district by offering comprehensive, free, equitable, and quality health services. This project will support one fixed health facility and one mobile/outreach team. The outreach team will reach five locations (3 IDP camps and two rural villages). Program implementation will involve both facility-based and outreach services. The project target population is 32,793 vulnerable individuals, including 6,558 men, 11,150 women, 7,392 boys, 7,693 girls, and 4,800 people with disabilities.ltbrgtThe program's activities are aligned with relevant strategic plans, including the Somalia NDP (2020-2024) and Somalia HNRP (2025). Our technical approach will bolster the resilience of crisis-affected communities, safeguarding mothers and children from morbidity and mortality by granting them access to quality essential services. Moreover, we will work on preventing disease outbreaks through awareness-raising and behavioral change strategies. This three-pronged approach is part of our strategy to address the immediate and medium-term needs of the population in distress by supporting public health facilities, the South West MOH, and the Qansah Dheere district health committee in implementing health interventions per available guidelines.ltbrgtWe will take deliberate steps to aid Somali communities in their journey towards self-reliance, achieved through capacity building of relevant ministries at the state, regional, and district levels. Additionally, we will intensify efforts to involve ministry officials in monitoring and supervising health facilities and program activities.ltbrgtHealth activities will prioritize critical life-saving interventions and disease prevention, encompassing the provision of essential health services, medical supplies, and equipment to ensure the uninterrupted delivery of quality care.ltbrgtOur program will provide an integrated package of six core components of EPHS to achieve desired health outcomes, including reducing maternal, neonatal, and child mortality rates, decreasing the rate of under-nutrition, and enhancing communicable and non-communicable disease surveillance and management, ultimately leading to an improved quality of life for the communities residing in Qansah Dheere district.ltbrgtWe will enhance access to and utilization of quality health services by delivering life-saving primary health care services, including essential PHC (EPHS) clinical care, child health care, immunization, treatment for communicable diseases, provision of essential medicines and supplies, sexual and reproductive health services (antenatal care, postnatal care, safe deliveries, dignity kits for pregnant mothers), and the establishment of referral pathways. We will conduct IPC health awareness, social mobilization, education, and advocacy activities to promote disease control, general well-being, and health and nutrition through 10 Community Health Workers (CHWs), ensuring that every level of the health pyramid receives adequate support.ltbrgtWe will adhere to EPHS guidelines to guide and monitor patients over time, ensuring the provision of a comprehensive array of health services across different levels. These guidelines aim to strengthen the links between homes, first-level facilities, and hospitals, ensuring that appropriate care is available at each stage. Health staff will be trained to offer GBV services, including clinical management of rape (CMR) and psychosocial support. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTarget Locations and GPSlt/pgtltpgt1.
